quote: I just had a couple of questions to build your design here for you. I've already got solar.
stewart_read: Customer reveals an existing system immediately, which should trigger orphaned_flow (ownership, installer, panel size, system working status). Rep does get ownership and attempts installer name, but never confirms panel size or working status until it surfaces unprompted at the very end.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be intentionally light on orphaned_flow probing to keep the call moving toward the battery-backup angle, which doesn't require full orphaned_flow detail.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to run the full orphaned_flow checklist (owns/leases, installer, panel size, system working) up front when a customer discloses existing solar — the 'is it working' question especially should not wait until the customer volunteers it at the goodbye.

quote: I can't remember right now what they called it. But k. No worries.
stewart_read: Customer can't recall the installer name and the rep immediately drops it with 'No worries' rather than trying a follow-up angle (approximate timeframe, monthly payment amount, or asking if paperwork is nearby) that might surface competitive intel.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: a genuine memory gap from an elderly customer may not be recoverable regardless of angle tried, so dropping it may have been the practical call.
coaching_implication: Low-stakes moment, but worth noting as a pattern: rep concedes on the first no rather than trying one alternate angle (e.g., 'no worries — do you remember about how much your payment is monthly?') which could still yield useful data for the closer.

quote: K. If you could actually take a photo of the bill and text it to me, I can just pull the information from the graph and put it directly into my system here.
stewart_read: The customer had just read the exact usage figure aloud verbally at 06:04 ('At 1,730.'), proving a viable read-back path existed. Instead the rep launched a photo-text process that consumed nearly six more minutes of struggle for an elderly, self-described slow-moving customer, directly missing the schema's 2-minute pivot rule.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: Ion's process may require the physical bill image (not just the number) for full design accuracy, so the rep's insistence on the photo could be procedurally correct even if slower.
coaching_implication: If a verbal number is already in hand and the customer shows early friction signs, cap the photo attempt at ~2 minutes before falling back to the number already given — reinforce the schema's elderly_low_tech_protocol time budget explicitly with this rep.

quote: Is it working, or is it giving you some trouble?
stewart_read: By this point roughly 4.5 minutes had elapsed since the photo request; the rep checks in but stays the course on the photo-text path rather than pivoting to the verbal number already captured, extending the friction past the schema's stated time budget.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: this reads as a genuine missed pivot point rather than a deliberate strategic hold — there's no evidence the rep is buying time for another reason.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to replay with the rep: 'you already had the number — here's where you should have said let's just use the number you gave me and moved on.'

quote: I have to check to see if I have any doctor's appointments. I got cancer.
stewart_read: This is a textbook vulnerability-disclosure trust gift per the schema, but the rep's response is a flat 'Yeah.' followed immediately by returning to scheduling logistics, with no acknowledgment of the health situation or a bridge to how the appointment fits around it.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be avoiding dwelling on the topic to not make the customer uncomfortable or derail the booking momentum.
coaching_implication: Coach a simple acknowledgment move here — 'I'm sorry to hear that, let's find a time that works around your appointments' — the schema explicitly flags this disclosure type as high-value to handle well, and the flat response risks the customer feeling unheard right as a cost objection follows.

quote: if it involves a lot of money, I don't have no time.
stewart_read: This is a cost objection directly tied to the customer's health/financial vulnerability. The rep responds with generic reassurance ('it doesn't cost a ton') rather than flipping the frame toward what the customer's CURRENT situation (existing loan payments, non-producing panels) is already costing him.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: no evidence the rep is deferring this deliberately for the closer — the response reads as a standard soft reassurance rather than a strategic hold.
coaching_implication: This objection recurs (see multi_touch_patterns) and never gets a real angle beyond reassurance — flag as the clearest missed inversion opportunity on the call.

stewart_read: Customer discloses his existing system has been covered in ice and non-producing for weeks — a DQ-relevant fact under orphaned_flow's 'is your system working' criterion. This surfaces only after the appointment is already locked, so it was never used to properly qualify or flag the lead for the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: since the appointment is already set and the rep is in wrap-up mode, raising a DQ question at 15:27 could unravel a booked call; letting it pass to the specialist could be a deliberate choice to not self-sabotage the sit.
coaching_implication: This fact needs to reach the closer regardless of when it surfaced — the handoff brief should flag 'system not producing, ice-covered for weeks' explicitly so the specialist walks in knowing this, rather than treating it as a throwaway parting comment.

quote: What I wanna do is find time for my energy specialist to give you a call and go through all the details and, you know, answer the questions you have about batteries.
stewart_read: This line itself is appropriately scoped (bridging to specialist), but it's included here as a positive contrast point — the rep correctly avoids explaining battery mechanics in depth despite opening the door to battery backup at 00:41-01:16, where she did explain some mechanism ('you're storing power in case there's a blackout... pull from the battery and protect your stuff from losing power').
coaching_implication: Note the early battery explanation at 01:04-01:16 as mild scope creep — brief and not damaging, but worth naming since the schema flags any unprompted feature/mechanism explanation as an anti-pattern under curiosity_over_features.
